name: Switzerland, canton of Zug

paths.name: Holding the portfolio personally (ordinary taxation)
paths.note: Dividends are ordinary income at the federal and the Zug progressive tariff (a portfolio holding under 10% gets no partial taxation); gains on listed shares are tax-free for a private investor (DBG art. 16 para. 3); annual cantonal and communal wealth tax on worldwide net assets; children inherit free of tax (StG ZG para. 175).

paths.name: Lump-sum taxation (Besteuerung nach dem Aufwand)
paths.note: Income and wealth tax are replaced by the ordinary tariffs applied to a deemed income of at least the cantonal minimum, 7 times the rent of the home or the living costs, and to a deemed wealth of at least 20 times that base (StG ZG para. 14, DBG art. 14). No time limit in law while both spouses stay non-Swiss and do not work in Switzerland. Foreign dividends and gains are covered; inheritance follows the ordinary Zug rules (children exempt).

checks.working: Inputs chosen so that taxable income is far above every tariff break; allowances, deductions (social deductions, child deductions) and the dividend-free part are ignored, as in the other recipes; a married couple with 3 children, no church tax, lives in the city of Zug, tax year 2026. DIVIDENDS 2,000,000, taxed in full (portfolio holding under 10%: DBG art. 20 para. 1 let. c, para. 1bis not met; StG ZG para. 19). Federal (DBG art. 36 para. 2, tariff in force since 1 Jan 2026): tax at 941,400 is 108,261.00, plus 11.50 per 100 above, = 11.5% of the whole amount: 2,000,000 x 11.5% = 230,000.00 (the CHF 263 per-child reduction of art. 36 para. 2bis, 789 in all, is ignored). Zug simple tax (StG ZG para. 35 para. 2, Mehrpersonentarif as indexed for 2025/26, 8.0% above 299,800): tax on the first 299,800 is 20,653.00 (sum of the 14 bands), so simple tax = 20,653.00 + 8% x (2,000,000 - 299,800) = 156,669.00. Multipliers 2026 (para. 2 para. 2b; Steuerfuesse 2023-2026): canton 78% + city of Zug 52% = 130%: 156,669.00 x 1.30 = 203,669.70. Total before credit 433,669.70. Flat-rate credit for the 15% treaty withholding on foreign dividends (Verordnung ueber die Anrechnung auslaendischer Quellensteuern, SR 672.201): 15% x 2,000,000 = 300,000.00, below the Swiss tax on those dividends. Dividend tax after credit 133,669.70. GAINS 1,000,000: nil, private capital gains on movable assets are tax-free (DBG art. 16 para. 3; StHG art. 7 para. 4 let. b). WEALTH 100,000,000 (para. 38, para. 44): exempt amounts 408,000 for the couple + 3 x 102,000 for the minor children = 714,000, taxable 99,286,000. Simple tax with the 2025/26 indexed bands (0.425 promille on the first 254,000, 0.85 on the next 254,000, 1.275 on the next 254,000, 1.7 above 762,000): 107.95 + 215.90 + 323.85 = 647.70, plus 1.7 promille x (99,286,000 - 762,000) = 167,490.80, = 168,138.50; x 1.30 = 218,580.05. Total 133,669.70 + 218,580.05 = 352,249.75.
checks.model_note: The engine applies one flat marginal rate of 21.9% (11.5% federal + 10.4% Zug) to every franc of dividends, whereas the Zug tariff is progressive below CHF 299,800: the law's tax is 3,331 of simple tax lower (x 1.30 = 4,330.30). The engine's wealth-tax bracket rates are also rounded to 5 decimals (0.00055 for 0.5525 promille etc.), worth +0.27.

checks.working: The tax does not depend on the actual dividends, gains or wealth (foreign income and foreign assets are covered), only on the deemed base, which this check ASSUMES to be a round CHF 1,000,000 (about 7 times a rent of CHF 12,000 a month; StG ZG para. 14 para. 3 let. b, and DBG art. 14 para. 3). The real base is a function of rent and living costs, see open questions. Ordinary tariffs on that base (StG ZG para. 14 para. 5; DBG art. 14 para. 5), married couple with 3 children, no church tax, tax year 2026. Federal (DBG art. 36 para. 2): 11.5% of 1,000,000 = 115,000.00 (108,261.00 at 941,400 + 11.50 per 100 on the 58,600 above); the per-child reduction of art. 36 para. 2bis (3 x 263 = 789) is NOT given to lump-sum taxpayers (DBG art. 14 para. 4: 'Die Ermässigung nach Artikel 36 Absatz 2bis zweiter Satz kommt nicht zur Anwendung'), so federal tax is 115,000.00. Zug income tax (para. 35 para. 2): simple tax 20,653.00 + 8% x (1,000,000 - 299,800) = 76,669.00; x (78% + 52%) = 99,669.70. Deemed wealth: at least 20 times the base (para. 14 para. 4) = 20,000,000, taxed as taxable wealth with no allowances: simple tax 647.70 + 1.7 promille x (20,000,000 - 762,000) = 33,352.30; x 1.30 = 43,358.99. Total 115,000.00 + 99,669.70 + 43,358.99 = 258,028.69.

Descendants are exempt from inheritance and gift tax in the canton of Zug whatever the amount (StG ZG para. 175 para. 1: the spouse, registered partner, direct descendants, step-children and parents of the deceased are exempt). There is no federal inheritance tax. Tax 0.

assumptions: The family is two non-Swiss spouses who have not been Swiss tax residents for 10 years and do not work in Switzerland, so lump-sum taxation is open to them (StG ZG para. 14 para. 1-2; DBG art. 14). Both must qualify.
City of Zug, tax year 2026: canton 78% (para. 2 para. 2b, 2026-2029) and commune 52%, no church tax. The national file's figures for Zug rest on the same 130% total.
Wealth-tax exemptions (CHF 714,000 for a couple with 3 minor children) are the 2025 indexed amounts published by the ESTV; the 2026 amounts were not published separately in the sources read.

A Swiss family foundation (ZGB art. 335) is not offered as a path. It is taxed as a legal entity (DBG art. 49) on its income and capital, its distributions are taxable income for the beneficiaries, and it can only serve education, endowment and support of family members; it brings no tax advantage over holding personally, and a mere holding company for a listed portfolio does not either (participation relief needs 10% stakes).

The lump-sum base is shown at the national-file representative of CHF 1,000,000. The family's actual base is the highest of the cantonal minimum (CHF 500,000), 7 times the rent or rental value of the home and the living costs; at the stated spending of EUR 400,000 and a rent of CHF 6,500 a month the base would be lower than CHF 1,000,000 and the lump sum correspondingly lower.
Treaty relief on foreign dividends is assumed to be claimed only if the control calculation stays below the lump sum; the 15% withholding is then a final cost, as for all other paths.
open_questions: Needs an engine change: the lump sum is a fixed amount per regime, but by law it is the tax on a base of at least the highest of the cantonal minimum, 7 times the rent and the family's worldwide living costs (StG ZG para. 14 para. 3; DBG art. 14 para. 3), which grows with rent and costs and is reassessed each year. The engine would need the base as a function of the family's spending and housing cost, with the ordinary tariffs applied to it.

Needs an engine change: modified lump sum. Claiming treaty-reduced withholding on foreign dividends puts that income into the control calculation, where it is taxed at the ordinary tariffs (StG ZG para. 14 para. 6 let. f, DBG art. 14 para. 4). The tax is then the higher of the lump sum and the control calculation, and a family with a large US-dominated portfolio that does not claim treaty relief bears 30% US withholding with no Swiss credit. The engine charges 15% on every foreign dividend and ignores the control calculation.

Needs an engine change: the Zug tariff is progressive, the engine uses a single marginal rate for dividends (about 4,300 too high on a CHF 2m income, and the federal marginal rate is 13% between CHF 152,400 and 941,300, not 11.5%). A progressive income tax per regime would remove the gap.

Tariff amounts indexed for 2026 should be confirmed against the Steuerverwaltung Zug's published 2026 Mehrpersonentarif and wealth-tax exemptions when they appear (the Grundtarif for 2026 is identical to 2025).

Lump sum for this family: the base is the highest of CHF 500,000 (Zug, Vo StG §4) / about CHF 435,000 (federal, DBG art. 14(3)), 7 times the rent or rental value of the home, and the family's world-wide living costs. For a CHF 5M home that is about CHF 1.2M; the tax file's representative CHF 1M base is close but not derived. An independent check on the legal minimum base gave about CHF 111,500 a year against CHF 257,000 here.
Tax file: the flat 11.5% federal rate overstates federal tax at the family's ~CHF 600,000 of dividends (average 10.5%, marginal 13%; ESTV tariff 2026).
